chinese_name: 空间 / 工程范围与工作内容

practice_categories.name: Employer Enabling Obligations
practice_categories.chinese_name: 业主 / 对方使能义务

performance_nodes.name: Employer design basis / Contractor design portions
performance_nodes.chinese_name: 业主设计基础 / 承包商设计部分
performance_nodes.logic: Red Book is based on Employer-designed Works. Employer provides Specifications / Drawings as the basis of the Works. Where the Contract specifies Contractor design portions, Contractor must submit Contractor’s Documents and comply with the Contract.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Main Performance Obligations > Employer design basis / Contractor design portions
secondary_paths: Time & Completion > EOT, only for 1.9 if express wording is verified
Claims, Determination & Disputes > Contractor claim, only for 1.9 if express wording is verified
elements: Employer-provided Specifications / Drawings define the Works
Contractor design only to the extent specified
Delayed drawings or instructions may affect performance

performance_nodes.name: Procurement
performance_nodes.logic: Procurement is part of Contractor’s delivery obligation. Contractor must procure / provide Plant, Materials, Contractor’s Documents, Contractor’s Personnel, Goods, consumables and other things and services required to fulfil its obligations.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Main Performance Obligations > Procurement
secondary_paths: Price & Payment > valuation / payment, only if payment issue arises
Risk & Protection > import / transport / third-party claims
elements: Goods as physical and logistical inputs
Packing, loading, transport, unloading, storage and protection
Customs clearance / permits / fees / import handling
Contractor’s Equipment dedicated to Works once on Site

performance_nodes.name: Execution of Works
performance_nodes.logic: Contractor’s core obligation is to execute and complete the Works and remedy defects in accordance with the Contract and Engineer’s instructions.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Main Performance Obligations > Execution of Works
secondary_paths: Claims, only where specific entitlement clause applies
elements: Co-operate with Employer’s Personnel and other contractors

performance_nodes.name: Compliance of completed Works
performance_nodes.logic: Scope is not only doing work. It is delivering completed Works that comply with the Contract, Specification, Drawings, quality, testing and defect-remedy requirements.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Main Performance Obligations > Compliance of completed Works

performance_nodes.name: Personnel
performance_nodes.logic: Contractor must organise Contractor’s Representative, staff and labour, and manage personnel capability, labour compliance, welfare, working hours, health and safety.
primary_clauses: Rates of Wages and Conditions of Labour
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Personnel
secondary_paths: Time & Completion if labour shortage affects progress

performance_nodes.name: Documents
performance_nodes.logic: Documents are a management instrument for performance: contract documents, Contractor’s Documents, progress reports, records, as-built records, O&M manuals, and claim evidence.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Documents

performance_nodes.name: Goods
performance_nodes.logic: Goods include Contractor’s Equipment, Materials, Plant and Temporary Works. Goods are physical and logistical inputs for the Works.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Goods
secondary_paths: Price & Payment if valuation issue arises

performance_nodes.name: Site including QHSE
performance_nodes.logic: This covers how Contractor controls the physical Site and construction environment: access routes, obstruction, security, environmental protection, temporary utilities, site operations, archaeological / geological findings, and QHSE.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Site including QHSE
secondary_paths: Time & Completion only where express EOT entitlement exists
Claims only where express Contractor claim exists

performance_nodes.name: Permits and approvals
performance_nodes.logic: Permits and approvals are split between Employer and Contractor. Employer obtains planning, zoning, building permits or other specified permits for the Permanent Works. Contractor obtains permits needed for its own performance, Goods delivery and import.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Permits and approvals
elements: Failure / delay in permits where expressly addressed

performance_nodes.name: Subcontracting
performance_nodes.logic: Subcontracting is a Scope management mechanism. It controls how Contractor delegates performance while remaining responsible.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Ancillary Management Obligations > Subcontracting
elements: Engineer prior consent to proposed Subcontractor
Deemed consent if Engineer gives no objection within 14 days
Contractor responsibility for acts/defaults of Subcontractors
Evidence of payment to nominated Subcontractor
Employer direct payment and deduction in next IPC

performance_nodes.name: Site access and possession
performance_nodes.logic: Employer must provide access and possession of the Site. If Employer fails to give access / possession within time and Contractor suffers delay and/or Cost, Contractor may be entitled subject to 20.2 to EOT and/or Cost Plus Profit, except where caused by Contractor’s own error or delay.
primary_clauses: Right of Access to the Site
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Site access and possession
secondary_paths: Claims, Determination & Disputes > Contractor claim for EOT / Cost
elements: Employer obligation to give access and possession

performance_nodes.name: Employer-supplied materials and equipment
performance_nodes.logic: Where the Specification provides for Employer-Supplied Materials or Employer’s Equipment, Employer makes them available for Contractor’s use. Contractor then has use / management obligations.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer-supplied materials and equipment

performance_nodes.name: Employer personnel and other contractors
performance_nodes.chinese_name: 管理本方人员及其他承包商
performance_nodes.logic: Employer must ensure Employer’s Personnel and other contractors cooperate with Contractor’s efforts and comply with relevant health / safety / environmental obligations. Contractor also has co-operation obligations under 4.6.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer personnel and other contractors
secondary_paths: Time & Completion if express EOT entitlement applies
elements: Unforeseeable co-operation instruction causing delay / Cost

performance_nodes.name: Employer permits
performance_nodes.logic: Employer-side permits are an enabling input. Employer obtains planning, zoning, building permits and other permits specified in the Specifications.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer permits
secondary_paths: Ancillary Management Obligations > Permits and approvals
elements: Indemnity for failures where expressly stated

performance_nodes.name: Employer assistance
performance_nodes.logic: Employer must provide reasonable assistance to allow Contractor to obtain relevant Laws, permits, permissions, licences, approvals, customs clearance and export approvals.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer assistance

performance_nodes.name: Site data and reference items
performance_nodes.chinese_name: 提供现场数据 / 参考点
performance_nodes.logic: Employer provides Site Data / Items of Reference. Contractor uses, interprets and verifies them. This node captures the interface between Employer-provided site information and Contractor’s setting out / physical condition risk.
primary_clauses: Site Data and Items of Reference
Agreement or Determination of Rectification Measures, Delay and/or Cost
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Site data and reference items
elements: Engineer agreement / determination of error and consequences

performance_nodes.name: Employer design documents
performance_nodes.logic: Employer’s Specifications and Drawings define the Works. Delayed drawings or instructions are Employer enabling failures that may affect time and cost.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer design documents
secondary_paths: Time & Completion > EOT, only for 1.9 if express wording exists
Claims > Contractor claim for EOT / Cost, only for 1.9 if express wording exists

performance_nodes.name: Engineer administration interface
performance_nodes.logic: Engineer is not a Scope obligation as such, but Engineer’s instructions, review, no-objection, agreement/determination and administration materially affect Scope performance.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Contract Mechanics > Engineer administration
secondary_paths: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Engineer administration interface

performance_nodes.name: Employer financial arrangements
performance_nodes.logic: Employer financial arrangements are mainly a Price & Payment / financial enablement issue. They can affect Contractor’s ability to continue Works, but should not be treated as core Scope unless linked to instruction, suspension, payment default or continuing performance issue.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Price & Payment > Employer financial arrangements
secondary_paths: Scope & Works > Employer Enabling Obligations > Employer financial arrangements

performance_nodes.name: Variation scope
performance_nodes.logic: Defines what can count as a Variation: quantity, quality, characteristics, levels, positions, dimensions, omission, additional work / Plant / Materials / services, and sequence / timing changes.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Variation scope

performance_nodes.name: Variation recognition dispute
performance_nodes.logic: This node captures disputes over whether an instruction, change, omission, quantity change, design clarification or Employer conduct legally constitutes a Variation.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Variation recognition dispute
elements: Whether there is an Engineer instruction
Whether the instruction changes the Works
Whether it is already Contractor’s original scope
Whether it is a compensable Variation

performance_nodes.name: Variation instruction
performance_nodes.logic: Variation by Instruction is the core mechanism. Engineer’s Instruction describes required changes. Contractor must comply before compensation is fixed. Contractor submits work details, programme modification / EOT and cost proposal within 28 days. Ordinary Variation adjustment is not treated as a Clause 20 claim.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Variation instruction
elements: No requirement to comply with 20.2 for ordinary Variation adjustment

performance_nodes.name: Variation proposal
performance_nodes.logic: Engineer may request a proposal before instructing a Variation. Contractor may submit a proposal or give reasons why it cannot comply. If Engineer does not consent and Contractor incurred Cost in submitting it, Contractor may be entitled subject to 20.2 to payment of such Cost.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Variation proposal
secondary_paths: Claims if proposal cost entitlement arises

performance_nodes.name: Variation EOT / Contract Price consequence
performance_nodes.chinese_name: 变更导致的工期 / 价款后果
performance_nodes.logic: This is the consequence layer of Variation. Under 13.3.1, Engineer proceeds under 3.7 to agree/determine EOT and/or Contract Price adjustment. Contractor is entitled to such EOT / adjustment without 20.2.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Variation EOT / Contract Price consequence

performance_nodes.name: Refusal to execute variation
performance_nodes.chinese_name: 拒绝履行 / 反对变更
performance_nodes.logic: Contractor is generally bound to execute each instructed Variation with due expedition and without delay. Contractor may promptly give Notice if varied work was unforeseeable having regard to scope/nature of Works, Contractor cannot readily obtain required Goods, or it adversely affects health/safety/environmental compliance. Engineer then cancels, confirms or varies the instruction.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Refusal to execute variation

performance_nodes.name: Daywork
performance_nodes.logic: Daywork is a Variation measurement / record mechanism. Contractor submits daily statements. If Engineer disagrees, Engineer proceeds under 3.7 to agree / determine resources.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Daywork

performance_nodes.name: Provisional Sum
performance_nodes.logic: Provisional Sums are specified by Employer for execution of part of the Works or supply of Plant, Materials or services. They are used only in accordance with Engineer’s instructions, and Contract Price is adjusted accordingly. They may also connect to nominated subcontractors.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Provisional Sum

performance_nodes.name: Change in Laws
performance_nodes.chinese_name: Change in Laws / 法律变化
performance_nodes.logic: Change in Laws can change the performance environment and may lead to EOT / Cost entitlement or price adjustment. It belongs in Scope Variables because it changes the legal conditions under which the Works are performed, but it also cross-links to Risk, Claims and Payment.
performance_nodes.primary_path: Scope & Works > Scope Variables and Variations > Change in Laws
elements: Change in Laws after Base Date

Claim for EOT: Right of Access to the Site
Claim for Cost: Right of Access to the Site

tag_reason_templates.Claim for Cost: Approved only where the existing Scope mapping identifies an express Contractor claim for Cost / Cost Plus Profit / additional payment; needs_lawyer_review remains.
tag_reason_templates.Contractor Breach / Default: Approved only for express Contractor failure / default / non-performance wording identified in the existing Scope mapping.
tag_reason_templates.Employer Breach / Default: Approved only for express Employer failure / default / non-performance wording identified in the existing Scope mapping.
tag_reason_templates.Determination: Approved where the Scope matrix expressly engages agreement or determination under Sub-Clause 3.7.
tag_reason_templates.Condition Precedent: Approved only for the express consent or prompt Notice gate identified in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Deemed Approval: Approved only for the express deemed-consent effect identified in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Deduction: Approved only for the express deduction from the next IPC identified in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Withholding: Approved only for the express right to withhold or refuse payment identified in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Indemnity: Approved only for the express indemnity element identified in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Remedy: Approved only where rejection or remedying defects is expressly addressed in the Scope matrix.
tag_reason_templates.Back-to-back: Approved only for the corresponding obligations / liabilities identified in the Scope matrix.
